667.t: Tonight Show, Milwaukee and Jackie's parents' upstairs flat
667.s: They leave Hollis, appear with Johnny Carson, go to Milwaukee, Roy stocks shelves in her father's IGA, and live in her parents' flat until the second child.
667.q: My parents had a house at that time. Yeah it was funny. My parents had a house at that time, that was a flat. And our lease was up in Hollis, which was on Long Island. We had moved from Philly to Long Island. And so when the lease was up, I was talking to my mother one night on the phone, and I was…

667.t: Leaving Riverdale and buying the Montclair house
667.s: The Nadelman son returns, they search for houses, and find their present home, moving in May 1, 1973.
667.q: I knew right away, I could see the quality of the house, and the way it was constructed. He did too.

459.s: Left for safety and family reasons, moving to a small town.
459.q: A combination. My daughter was eight going towards nine at the time, and I said, “Krissy keeps complaining that she has to yell up at me where we live to come down and get her” because it wasn’t safe I guess. Well I was a typical Lebanese father. I’m very protective of my children, or my child. I…

459.s: Joe Corello got him a band and a house in Syracuse.
459.q: I says, “Joey, I’m retiring.” He says, “Come to Syracuse, I’ll get you a band.” He knew that was the first thing in my life.

435.s: The uprooting from Oakland to a rented house arranged through Columbia Records and Irving Townsend.
435.q: Well that was a real uprooting. I remember it very clearly because it was 1960, it was a presidential year. Kennedy was elected. Kennedy ran against Nixon and won. Barry Goldwater was a big name in those days. And for me that just flags up so many historical things. But mainly what I remember was…

1025.t: Why he chose Toronto in the mid-1960s
1025.s: Canada welcomed educated immigrants, Toronto was British-influenced and near New York.
1025.q: Oh I guess I did, it’s hard to recall. I obviously didn’t just wake up one morning and say well I’m going to Canada. I thought about it, and a lot of people have said why Toronto? And to put it all in perspective, in the mid-60s if you had a half decent education and if you were qualified in some…

796.t: Relocating east and then to the Poconos; Bob Dorough
796.s: Moving to New York with a family, then choosing the Poconos in 1970 after visiting Bob Dorough, who became a close friend and mentor.
796.ch: Poconos and the Phil Woods era begins
796.q: More of a lifestyle decision. We had lived in California, I grew up there. I lived in my old neighborhood and we had a house. And we got to New York and we didn’t have a house and I was married and had a child, and we, you know we just did sublets or staying with

562.t: Moving to San Diego after Denver
562.s: After graduate school in Colorado she chose San Diego over New York, and works with a fine local rhythm section.
562.ch: San Diego and working as a flutist
562.q: Friends, actually not in the music field, feeling that I needed to live on one of the coasts for work, and after graduate school I was living in Denver because I went to the University of Northern Colorado for graduate. And Denver was definitely not the place. It has an emphasis on other kinds of…

59.t: Living in Florida; New York versus the West Coast
59.s: He now lives in Florida and sees himself fundamentally as a New York musician.
59.ch: Organ work, singers and Russia tour
59.q: Well I’ve never been really a west coast musician although I have done some film work there and occasional appearances. I’m still a New York musician fundamentally. I really couldn’t make a comparison, and wouldn’t do that question justice.

594.t: Moving to San Diego to be near his mother
594.s: He lived in New York until about 1978, then moved to San Diego for his mother, married there, and travels for work.
594.q: Yeah, I lived in New York up until around 1978. And then I moved to San Diego. And the reason I moved was because my mom still lives here, and I’m an only child, she was getting on in age and I thought I should be with her and hang out with her. So I actually came out just with the intentions of…

1033.s: She wants theater, a big band record and orchestral work; she moved upstate after having a baby.
1033.q: You know you can’t think too long term in this business because everything is changing constantly. I have things that I really want to do. You know I really want to do theater again. I really want to make a big band record. I really want to do more orchestral work. At some point I want to do a…

756.t: Why he stayed in Rome rather than moving to New York
756.s: After the Rawls years he came home when Jill was pregnant, found plenty of work and values the variety of gigs possible in a smaller market.
756.ch: Staying in Rome and best and worst gigs
756.q: Yeah I wanted to move to New York. And at the end of the Lou Rawls days I probably should have stayed out in Las Vegas or in LA, and I had a lot of opportunities to do things, but you know, I was married and then Jill got pregnant and I came home and made a go of it here.

585.t: Getting visa and citizenship; the value of travel
585.s: The easier 1994 scene, a club-date sponsor and 01 visa, the citizenship paperwork about travel history, and how travel changes her perspective.
585.ch: Work, pay and the New York life
585.q: Yes. Because even when I first came here and I was doing gigs on Broadway, there was still a happening studio scene in New York. There were still things going on. I mean I think that time in New York was really great. I got hooked up with a whole corporate party scene at the end of ’94, and I got…

947.t: Moving to the U.S. and great Canadian artists
947.s: Shaffer says coming to the U.S. seemed a fantasy and happened through fortuitous circumstances; he discusses Canadian stars.
947.q: Well yes. It seemed like a fantasy though, very difficult, I was aware, to do, to get the kind of credentials you needed to work legally in the U.S. as a Canadian. But it wasn’t like it is today. Certainly we look at today’s musical artists and we see that some of the top, absolute top tier…

932.t: Why Los Angeles instead of New York
932.s: He chose L.A. for lifestyle and the capital of film and TV scoring.
932.q: Well one is the lifestyle. I didn’t want to have to share bathrooms with people in an apartment that’s four by eight. Yeah, and you really have to live in Manhattan. You can’t really live in Queens or Brooklyn. I know some people live in Brooklyn and New Jersey, but if you get a call and you need…

1005.t: Moving to America and admiring American players
1005.s: He stayed in Italy until marrying at 33, then moved to the US to learn from exceptional musicians; in Milan they revered American jazz players such as Tommy Flanagan and Barry Harris.
1005.q: Well it’s hard to say. Because I’ll tell you something very funny. When I was still living with my parents, you know, I used to say — you know I stayed with my parents until I got married. I have nothing against this. You know here in America most of the kids, when they go to college they leave…

834.t: Moving to Seattle, Heaven and Hell, and the sabbatical miniatures
834.s: He married, had kids, moved to Seattle after 24-25 years in Manhattan, and composed Heaven and Hell for a tentet; then taught at Cornish for 15 years.
834.q: That was a little earlier. “Heaven and Hell” was from when I moved to – well I moved – so I’ll make it really quick. All those various things I was doing, that was in New York, go to Europe, back and forth, go blah-blah-blah. Then I got married, then I had kids, then I had two kids. And trying to…

618.t: Choosing San Francisco over New York
618.s: He found New York too intense, disliked the weather, and fell in love with San Francisco during a 1963 fellowship at Langley Porter.
618.q: I toyed with it. In some ways it would have been easier to keep a higher profile musical career going had I stayed in New York. But back then the vibe in New York I found too intense and oppressive. I have plenty of internal energy. I don’t need that press from outside so much. And I hated the…

110.s: What was meant to be a year in Wilton became permanent, thanks to better schools, New York proximity and Irving Townsend's house.
110.q: We came for a year. I talked the wife, Iola, and the family into making a move, and we’d go back to our wonderful home in Montclair, outside of Oakland.

504.t: Moving to the Woodstock area and having the house built
504.s: They moved upstate in the early 1970s, rented in Mt. Tremper, and then had a simple house built from scratch.
504.ch: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
504.q: Well it had to have been in the early 70’s, because Minya our daughter was born up here around that period. We’ve been up here over thirty-five, maybe almost forty years.

371.t: Why Jones moved to Hartwick, New York
371.s: Hank and Teddy found the farm while driving on days off from CBS, and he once planned to be a gentleman farmer.
371.ch: Hartwick and the CBS staff years
371.q: On my days off at CBS, which were few and far between, Teddy and I would hop in my car even after we got off the show at night, and go around looking for places. This was just one of the many places that we visited. We visited Pennsylvania, New Hampshire, you name it! We settled on this place…

108.t: Choosing to stay in New York
108.s: He enjoyed staff work and was able to raise his family in New York.
108.q: I enjoyed it as much as I did doing the other things, and the fact that I didn’t have to run all over the country enhanced my acceptance of it. I just took it as it came.

165.t: Moving to Sausalito and Mill Valley
165.s: After years at Monterey they moved to a Sausalito houseboat and then bought a 1905 house in Mill Valley.
165.q: We went to San Francisco, which through coming to the Monterey Festival every year for five years, we would always talk the rest of the year – like we’d stay there a month. We’d do Monterey and then rent a house or some kind of cabin up in Big Sur or somewhere around there, spend the rest of the…

505.t: Burned out on New York at thirty
505.s: He left New York because his life was out of control from drugs and women after six years of Miles, Elvin and Lookout Farm.
505.ch: A&M, Indian music and the California fusion attempt
505.q: And that’s years later. But even then, in that period, Chick was that thing. Weather Report was that thing. That was that period. I didn’t find the right formula. I wanted to, as I said, for personal reasons. Some of it was musical reasons. But it got me out of New York, and that is – the upshot…

555.t: The 1979 Kansas City festival, St. Lucia and settling in New York
555.s: Two women wanted her at the 1979 Kansas City festival, she finished in Jamaica, visited a friend in St. Lucia, and bought an apartment in New York.
555.q: I had a friend who’s there from [St. Lucia]. He was in Jamaica studying with me and so I went to his hometown and just hung out there for a while.

228.t: Persuading Dollie to move to Hartford
228.s: Dollie, a staunch New Yorker, resisted until McLean found a house and an Atheneum job for her; he took a Hartford Dispensary counseling job.
228.ch: Hartford, prison, theater and the Collective
228.q: That’s where they started me on that. I went around and met Cheryl Smith, the lady you met yesterday, and a few other people, and Dollie and I. We started meeting. We started talking about – well, that’s later on. First I started meeting some people and commuting back and forth. So I looked up, and…

376.t: Buying the Montauk house after Yonkers
376.s: Neighbors in Yonkers took them to Montauk, where they bought a house.
376.q: It was… We went… Well, I’ll tell you this story. I tell you just about everything, the truth. You’ll see what is useable or of interest. We were living in Yonkers. And uh…

17.ch: Life in Columbus and recent activity
17.q: Yeah, about 17 years, Bill, and I've become very acquainted with the town and I like it very much. And of course this would be my senior year at Capital University, it's very relaxing here, it's a nice town, you know, just, it isn't that knock-down, drag-out, bam bam bam, like New York, you know. 115.s: His wife liked Denver, so he moved there in 1973, ahead of many.
115.ch: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
115.q: Well, the first time I came out, and then I came out again and I brought my wife.

78.t: Why Benny Morton avoided the road
78.s: Morton, a New Yorker attached to his mother, disliked one-nighters and stayed in demand for New York recording work.
78.ch: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
78.q: mother a lot. I don't think Benny ever married, in fact, unless it's been recently. He was single, but he just never liked the hazards of traveling.
